name: Michigan
note: In Michigan the funeral director who first takes custody of the body reports the death through the state's web-based registration system, and the death record must be certified and filed with the local registrar within 72 hours; the physician (or the county medical examiner in referred cases) has 48 hours to certify the cause. The local registrar transmits the record to the state registrar, and a certified copy of a death record, cause of death included, is available to any applicant. Onward, county clerks must cancel deceased electors in the qualified voter file at least monthly, and the Secretary of State uses the Social Security death master file both to cancel driver's licences and to purge the voter file. Social Security and other federal notifications are in the us-federal layer.

steps.title: Report the discovery of a body
steps.who: Any individual who discovers a body they know or have reason to know is dead.
steps.summary: A person who finds a body must tell a law enforcement agency, a funeral home or a 9-1-1 operator unless they know one has already been told. Failing to do so is a misdemeanor, and a felony if done to conceal the fact or cause of death.

steps.title: Pronounce death
steps.who: A physician or registered nurse; a licensed health facility may decide which of its medical personnel may pronounce.
steps.trigger: Irreversible cessation of circulatory and respiratory functions, or of all brain functions.
steps.summary: Michigan's Determination of Death Act lets a physician or a registered nurse pronounce death in accordance with accepted medical standards.

steps.title: Notify the county medical examiner of a reportable death
steps.who: A physician, the individual in charge of a hospital or institution, or any other individual with first knowledge of the death.
steps.trigger: A sudden, unexpected, accidental, violent or suspicious death; a death without medical attendance in the preceding 48 hours (unless the attending physician can determine the cause); or a death resulting from an abortion.
steps.summary: Reportable deaths go to the county medical examiner, who must investigate the cause and manner of death in cases of violence, unexpected death, death without recent medical attendance, and abortion-related death.

steps.title: Certify the medical cause of death
steps.who: Outside an institution: the physician in charge of the decedent's care for the fatal illness, or an authorized representative physician. In an institution: the attending physician or, in their absence, an authorized representative, the institution's chief medical officer, or a pathologist.
steps.trigger: The funeral director presents the death record for medical certification.

deadline.text: not later than 48 hours after death

steps.summary: The certifier completes the medical certification portion of the death record within 48 hours, and may not neglect or refuse to certify when properly presented. Certifiers must be trained on the web-based system, and electronic submission of the medical certification becomes mandatory one year after the 2026 amendment.

steps.title: Medical examiner certifies cause in investigated deaths
steps.trigger: An investigation is required under MCL 52.202.

deadline.text: within 48 hours after taking charge of the case

steps.summary: Where an investigation is required, the medical examiner determines the cause of death and signs the medical certification within 48 hours. If the cause cannot be determined in time, the funeral director is told why and final disposition waits for authorization.

steps.title: File the death record with the local registrar
steps.who: The funeral director who first assumes custody of the body (or an authorized agent), with personal data from the next of kin or best qualified source; the record is certified by a licensed funeral director.
steps.summary: The funeral director reports the death through the department's web-based registration system and files the certified record with the local registrar of the district of death within 72 hours. The state registrar may extend time periods in cases of undue hardship. Wilfully refusing to provide required vital records information is a misdemeanor.

steps.title: Obtain authorization for final disposition
steps.who: The local registrar (or state registrar) signs the authorization; for cremation the county medical examiner must also sign.
steps.trigger: The funeral director's request after taking custody.

deadline.text: not later than 72 hours after death or finding of the body, and before disposition

steps.summary: Burial or other disposition requires an authorization on a state form signed by a registrar, obtained within 72 hours and before disposition. Every cremation authorization must also be signed by the medical examiner of the county of death.

steps.title: Local registrar transmits the record to the state
steps.who: The local registrar (county clerk, or a city clerk or department designated for a city).
steps.trigger: Acceptance of the death record for registration.
steps.summary: The local registrar examines and accepts each record and transmits it to the department in the manner the state registrar prescribes. The state registrar is custodian of the only system of vital statistics in the state.

steps.title: State forwards non-resident deaths to the county of residence
steps.trigger: A registered death of a person who died outside their county of residence.
steps.summary: The state registrar sends the necessary information monthly to the local registrar of the decedent's county of residence, who may not issue certified copies from it.

steps.title: Certified copies of the death record
steps.who: The state registrar or a local registrar, to any applicant.
steps.trigger: A written request and the prescribed fee.
steps.summary: Michigan death records are open: a certified copy, including the cause of death, is issued to any applicant on written request and payment of the fee.

steps.title: Data to the national vital statistics agency
steps.who: The Department of Health and Human Services.
steps.trigger: Registration; under cost-sharing arrangements with the federal agency.
steps.summary: The department may furnish copies or data to the federal agency responsible for national vital statistics, for statistical use only unless the state registrar authorises otherwise.

steps.title: County clerk cancels deceased voters in the qualified voter file
steps.who: Each county clerk, followed by the Secretary of State and the city or township clerk.
steps.trigger: Deaths in the county of individuals over 17 1/2.

deadline.text: at least monthly, by the second business day of each month (weekly, then daily, before August and November elections)

steps.summary: County clerks update the statewide qualified voter file at least monthly to start cancelling the registrations of everyone who died in the county. Within 24 hours the Secretary of State notifies the city or township clerk, who completes the cancellation and spoils any absent voter ballot already returned.

steps.title: Secretary of State cancels driver's licences using the SSA death master file
steps.who: The Michigan Secretary of State, using information from the Social Security Administration's death master file.
steps.trigger: Receipt of death master file information about a Michigan resident.
steps.summary: Michigan's election law refers to the process by which the Secretary of State uses the SSA death master file to cancel the operator's or chauffeur's licence or state ID card of a deceased resident. The licence cancellation itself rests on the Vehicle Code, which was not read.

steps.title: Death master file data also purges the voter file
steps.trigger: Death master file information used for licence cancellation.
steps.summary: The same death master file information must be used at least monthly to cancel the voter registration of electors found to be deceased, and the cancellations are made available to county, city and township clerks.

steps.title: Verification of the facts of a death for any person
steps.who: The state registrar or a local registrar.
steps.trigger: A written request and the prescribed fee.
steps.summary: Any person may have the registrar verify the name, the nature, date and place of the event, and the date of filing. Together with open certified copies, this gives banks and insurers a way to confirm a death without the family.

steps.title: Vital statistics data to public or private agencies
steps.who: The Department of Health and Human Services.
steps.trigger: A request, on terms the department prescribes.
steps.summary: The department may furnish copies or data to federal, state, local and other public or private agencies for statistical or administrative purposes, for the requested purpose only.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: The certified death record must be filed with the local registrar within 72 hours after the death; the medical certification is due within 48 hours.

informantDuty.note: The funeral director who first assumes custody reports the death, obtaining personal data from the next of kin or best qualified source.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review of every certificate. The county medical examiner certifies only investigated deaths, but must sign every cremation authorization.

electronicRegistration.note: The funeral director's report must be submitted through the department's web-based system; electronic submission of the medical certification becomes mandatory one year after the 2026 amendment (2026 PA 3, effective 17 March 2026), i.e. from about March 2027.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No population register; the state registrar keeps the single state system of vital statistics.

governmentPropagation.note: County clerks purge the qualified voter file monthly and the Secretary of State uses the SSA death master file for licences and voter records; Social Security notification is in the federal layer.

certificateAccess.note: A certified copy of a death record, including the cause of death, is issued to any applicant.

privateSectorVerification.note: Any person may obtain a verification of the facts of a death or a certified copy; the department may also furnish data to private agencies on its own terms. There is no statutory duty on banks or insurers.

gaps: The Michigan Vehicle Code provision under which the Secretary of State cancels a deceased person's driver's licence was not located; the step rests on MCL 168.509o(4), which describes that process.

No Michigan statute was found requiring the state registrar to send death data to SSA (EDR/EVVE feeds), the Department of Treasury, or state Medicaid; any such feeds are administrative and not sourced here.

MCL 333.2843(2)'s one-year phase-in of electronic medical certification runs from 'the effective date of the amendatory act that added this sentence'; the history line suggests 2026 PA 3 (immediate effect 17 March 2026) but the act itself was not read.
Probate notice to creditors (EPIC) was not researched as a public-notice step.
MCL 333.2849 and 333.2840 returned 404 on legislature.mi.gov (sections apparently do not exist).
